source_gaps: Windows 11: the page does not name the exact toggle for an app's notifications; it says 'Turn notifications on or off' and the page lists Windows 10 and 11 under Applies To without separate Windows 11 steps. Chrome: the page gives no steps for changing or removing a site that is already allowed, so no candidate covers that. Android: the page says settings can vary by phone, so labels may differ. All pages were read through a summarising WebFetch; wording was checked against the fetch output, not character by character.

source_refs.title: Turn notifications on or off for a specific app on your iPhone - Apple Support
source_refs.section: Turn notifications on or off for a specific app
source_refs.applicability: iPhone; the Notifications option may not appear if the app cannot send notifications
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Select Notifications. If it doesn't appear, the app may not be able to send notifications.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone: Open Settings and select 'Apps.' Select the app you want to change. Select 'Notifications.' If it doesn't appear, the app may not be able to send notifications. Turn 'Allow Notifications' off or on.

source_refs.title: Control notifications on Android - Android Help
source_refs.section: Turn off notifications for one app (Settings app)
source_refs.applicability: Android; labels can vary by phone
source_refs.verified_excerpt: You can turn off all notifications for a listed app or choose from specific categories.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Android: Open your device's 'Settings' app. Tap 'Notifications', and then 'App notifications'. Under 'Most recent', find the app. To find more apps, tap the dropdown menu and choose 'All apps'. Tap the app. Turn the app's notifications off. You can turn off all notifications for a listed app or choose from specific categories.

source_refs.title: Control notifications on Android - Android Help
source_refs.section: Older Android versions and app categories
source_refs.applicability: Android; applies only when 'Most recent' does not appear
source_refs.verified_excerpt: If you don't see Most recent, you're probably on an older Android version.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On older Android versions: If you don't see 'Most recent', you're probably on an older Android version. In that case, tap 'App notifications', then tap an app. You can turn off notifications, notification dots, and notification categories there. If the app has categories, tap a category for more options.

source_refs.title: Notifications and Do Not Disturb in Windows - Microsoft Support
source_refs.section: Turn off notifications for a specific app
source_refs.applicability: Windows 11; the page's Applies To line lists Windows 11 and Windows 10 and gives no separate Windows 11 steps; the per-app toggle label is not named
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Select the app under Notifications from apps and other senders.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Windows 11: Open Start, then go to Settings > System > Notifications. Select the app under Notifications from apps and other senders. Turn notifications on or off: disable notifications for specific apps if you no longer want to receive them.

source_refs.title: Use notifications to get alerts - Computer - Google Chrome Help
source_refs.section: Block a website from sending notifications
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Next to Not allowed to send notifications, click Add.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On a computer in Chrome: Open Chrome on your computer. At the top right, click 'More', then 'Settings'. Select 'Privacy and security', then 'Site Settings', then 'Notifications'. Next to 'Not allowed to send notifications,' click 'Add'. Enter the website's address, then click 'Add'.

source_refs.title: Use notifications to get alerts - Computer - Google Chrome Help
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Click Settings, then Don't allow to deny it.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On a computer in Chrome: When a site asks for permission, a 'Get notifications?' message appears at the top of the browser. Click 'Settings', then 'Don't allow' to deny it.
